abstract: BACKGROUND: Many transfusion reactions are not reported to hemovigilance systems, and the features needed to recognize them are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. We sought to develop and evaluate an open-source, multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline to extract transfusion reaction features defined by the National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Hemovigilance Module from clinical notes. METHODS: We curated 181 features from the NHSN protocol and developed a multi-stage pipeline that extracted features, their timing, and clinical details from free-text notes. Three open-weight large language models (Qwen 3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Kimi K3) were applied to 50 notes from expert-written scenarios, published case reports, and MIMIC-IV discharge summaries. Two physicians independently evaluated every model output in a blinded interface. The primary analysis was restricted to feature occurrences with concordant physician assessments. RESULTS: Physicians agreed on 1,201 of 1,343 co-rated feature occurrences (89.4%; Krippendorff's alpha 0.73). Precision was above 0.98 for all models. Sensitivity was 0.774 (95% CI 0.745-0.800) for Kimi K3, 0.636 (0.604-0.667) for GPT-OSS-120B, and 0.624 (0.593-0.655) for Qwen 3.6-27B, and specificity ranged from 0.952 to 0.991. Omissions accounted for more than 94% of false negatives. Timing and clinical details were judged supported or reasonable in more than 92% and 97% of assessments, respectively. Results were consistent across note sources and in analyses including discordant assessments. CONCLUSION: Multi-agent AI pipelines provide a feasible method for extracting transfusion reaction signals from clinical notes with high precision. Our work may have applications in active hemovigilance, reaction classification, and big data research.

abstract: Emerging Plasmodium falciparum resistance to frontline artemisinin (ART) derivatives threatens global malaria control efforts. abstract: Gait analytics is utilized for a wide range of health-related applications, ranging from fitness tracking to medical diagnostics, and beyond. Inertial measurement units that are ubiquitously available in mobile devices provide an accessible means of gait analysis but differences in sensor specifications, placement, and recording protocols limit comparability across studies. Comparability varied across datasets and sensor configurations, with correlation coefficients between average gait cycles ranging from 0.5 to close to 1.0. Centrally positioned sensors generally show greater correspondence than peripheral sensors, although differences in statistical features persist even between sensors at nominally identical locations. The proposed open-source framework implemented in Python provides a foundation for reproducible cross-study gait analysis and for investigating residual heterogeneity associated with datasets and sensor configurations.

abstract: Objective: To identify community - prioritized metadata for reporting and sharing computable phenotypes (CPs), develop a cross-library candidate framework, assess alignment between user requirements and library metadata, and test the feasibility of metadata exchange. The consortium performed a cross-library field comparison and literature review to inform candidate fields, refined through consortium consensus. The community approach was developed through stakeholder interviews, a survey, and workshop, guided by a working group. Community requirements were interpretively mapped to the resulting framework and classified into conformance tiers. abstract: Machine-learning models based on routine laboratory panels can predict outcomes but can be difficult to interpret and operationalize. We present COMBIO, an automated pipeline that distils such a model into a compact closed-form biomarker. The composite is a product of laboratory measurements raised to integer powers from minus two to two. The sign of each exponent indicates whether higher values of the corresponding measurement increase or decrease the composite. Shapley additive explanation values from the gradient-boosted reference model rank five candidate measurements and guide eligible exponent signs. An exhaustive search over small integer exponents selects the formula on an inner validation set, before evaluation on the reserved test set. We evaluated COMBIO across six tasks: three National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey outcomes, liver-disease classification in the Indian Liver Patient Dataset, and Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV in-hospital mortality and sepsis case-finding, with external evaluation in the eICU Collaborative Research Database for the two hospital tasks. Across the six test sets, COMBIO's area under the receiver operating characteristic curve differed by at most 0.03 from logistic regression using the five candidate laboratory measurements. The hospital mortality composite had an area under the curve of 0.698 in the external database. A version restricted to widely available measurements in the source hospital database achieved an area under the curve of 0.786 in a cohort covering 92% of admissions. The multiplicative representation provides compactness rather than additional accuracy, and local validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

abstract: In the healthcare sector, claim denials impose significant financial and administrative burdens, emphasizing the need for automated and trustworthy decision-support systems. This paper proposes a modular Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for healthcare claim denial analysis, integrating specialized agents for denial risk prediction, risk factor identification, diagnosis-procedure-medication code relationship analysis, and counterfactual analysis. The framework integrates predictive analytics, graph-based learning, a Hybrid Contextual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline grounded in healthcare policy documents, and a dedicated HIPAA Compliance Agent to support privacy protection. Evaluated on a synthetic healthcare claims dataset, the framework achieved 98% traceability of reported numerical findings, validated 214 of 216 policy citations, and removed all 280 identified sensitive identifiers without modifying the underlying analysis. These findings pave the way for further research into Agentic AI as a framework for explainable, policy-aware, and privacy-preserving healthcare claim denial management.

abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in high-risks decision-making systems across domains such as healthcare, finance, and the judicial system. As reliance on predictive models grows, so does the demand for Explainable AI (XAI) to ensure transparency, trust, and interpretability. However, existing XAI approaches often fail to present explanations in a format accessible to domain experts, limiting their practical utility. Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a bridge between complex models and end-users, offering natural language explanations. Yet, their use introduces new risks, including hallucinated outputs and lack of source traceability. To address these challenges, we propose a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) that not only combines standard predictive models with XAI techniques but also incorporates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation module as an interactive enhancer. This module grounds explanations in verified medical knowledge, reformulates technical outputs into a human-like format, and enables users-such as clinicians-to actively query the system. By fostering an interactive, human-in-the-loop environment, our approach empowers domain experts to explore model decisions, contextualize explanations, and build trust in AI-assisted diagnostics. The study concludes with preliminary experiments validating the proposed methodology.

key_points: 附加参数不足1.5%

abstract: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts. Human vision, by contrast, remains robust under these conditions, a property partly attributed to the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex, which refines visual information over time. Inspired by this, we append lightweight recurrent refinement blocks to segmentation backbones, namely Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and study their behaviour as the number of iterations increases at test time (including beyond the training horizon). Evaluated on two open-source datasets, Kvasir- SEG and ARCADE, our recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters and yield gains on clean data (up to 1.4 pp) and under noise (up to 17 pp) while reducing HD95. Code is available at https://github.com/joaodsmarques/recurrencehelpsegmentation .
zh_abstract: 尽管前馈分割网络在大型队列上表现良好，但在训练样本少且存在成像伪影的受限临床场景中，其性能会下降。相比之下，人类视觉在这些条件下依然稳健，这一特性部分归因于视觉皮层的循环和反馈连接，它们可随时间对视觉信息进行精炼。受此启发，我们在分割骨干网络后附加轻量级循环精炼模块，即条件随机场（Conditional Random Fields, CRFs）、现代Hopfield网络（modern Hopfield networks）和卷积GRU（convolutional GRUs），并研究其在测试时随迭代次数增加（包括超出训练迭代范围）的行为。在Kvasir-SEG和ARCADE两个开源数据集上的评估显示，我们的循环模块增加的参数不足1.5%，在干净数据上带来提升（最高1.4个百分点），在噪声条件下带来提升（最高17个百分点），同时降低了HD95。代码见 https://github.com/joaodsmarques/recurrencehelpsegmentation 。

abstract: Background: Binary hypotension forecasts do not describe the depth and duration of future low pressure. Burden forecasts may support graded early warning, but better forecast scores need not yield more useful alerts. Objective: To evaluate conditional quantiles of the next 15-minute mean arterial pressure (MAP) deficit below 65 mmHg and distinguish forecasting performance from episode-warning performance. Methods: Public VitalDB numeric arterial MAP was reduced to 10-second medians without forward filling. Subject-disjoint training, validation and test splits included 70,402, 14,270 and 15,575 labeled windows. We compared climatology, calibrated persistence, last-MAP-only boosting, and direct and residual quantile boosting, with and without additional MAP-history features. Patient-weighted pinball loss and subject-bootstrap intervals evaluated forecasting. Validation selected alert thresholds before a hash-recorded test evaluation. Results: In the test split, the prespecified residual-versus-persistence comparison at the 90th percentile yielded losses of 2.256 and 2.900 mmHg-min, respectively (difference -0.644; 95% interval -0.814 to -0.487). Direct prediction achieved 2.196, and direct prediction with additional MAP features achieved 2.193. Episode-warning results were sensitive to the alert rule and operating threshold. Conclusions: This retrospective benchmark separates burden-forecast skill from warning-policy performance. Findings support further study of direct burden estimation; they do not establish patient benefit, prospective reliability or transportability beyond the source hospital.
zh_abstract: 【背景】二元低血压预测无法描述未来低血压的深度和持续时间。负荷（burden）预测可能有助于分级早期预警，但预测评分更好并不一定带来更有用的警报。【目的】评估未来15分钟内平均动脉压（MAP）低于65 mmHg的不足量的条件分位数，并区分预测性能与发作预警性能。【方法】将公开的VitalDB有创动脉MAP数值数据处理为10秒中位数，不做前向填充。按受试者互不重叠划分的训练集、验证集和测试集分别包含70,402、14,270和15,575个已标注窗口。我们比较了气候学基线（climatology）、校准持续性预测（calibrated persistence）、仅使用最近一次MAP的提升（boosting）模型，以及直接分位数提升和残差分位数提升模型，每种均分别在有和没有额外MAP历史特征的情况下进行。预测评估采用按患者加权的pinball损失和按受试者自助法（bootstrap）得到的区间。在记录哈希值的测试评估之前，由验证集选定警报阈值。【结果】在测试集中，预先设定的第90百分位数残差模型与持续性预测的比较显示，损失分别为2.256和2.900 mmHg·min（差值-0.644；95%区间-0.814至-0.487）。直接预测的损失为2.196，加入额外MAP特征的直接预测为2.193。发作预警结果对警报规则和操作阈值较为敏感。【结论】这一回顾性基准研究将负荷预测技能与预警策略性能区分开来。研究结果支持进一步研究直接负荷估计；但并不能证明对患者有益，也不能证明前瞻性可靠性，或在来源医院之外的可迁移性。

reason: 预印本，理论方法有新意但医疗证据有限，属增量档
abstract: Machine learning based segmentation models are frequently miscalibrated, producing for each pixel a label prediction whose associated confidence does not accurately reflect the true underlying probability. This limitation is particularly critical in high-stakes applications such as medical image segmentation. Although several calibration methods have been proposed, only a small subset of them provides theoretical guarantees on the calibration error, i.e., they do not typically ensure that, with high probability, the model exhibits a low calibration error. In this work, we develop a post-hoc calibration method for which formal calibration guarantees can be established. To achieve this, we derive from standard concentration inequalities an improved theoretical bound that explicitly accounts for the spatial dependence inherent in binary segmentation outputs. We empirically demonstrate that the proposed calibrator satisfies the derived guarantee and outperforms existing post-hoc calibration approaches.
zh_abstract: 基于机器学习的分割模型经常存在校准不良的问题，即为每个像素给出的标签预测，其相应置信度并不能准确反映真实的潜在概率。这一局限在医学图像分割等高风险应用中尤为关键。尽管已有多种校准方法被提出，但其中只有一小部分能对校准误差提供理论保证，即它们通常无法确保模型以高概率表现出较低的校准误差。在本工作中，我们提出了一种可建立形式化校准保证的事后（post-hoc）校准方法。为此，我们从标准集中不等式出发，推导出一个改进的理论界，明确考虑了二值分割输出中固有的空间依赖性。我们通过实验证明，所提出的校准器满足所推导的保证，并且优于现有的事后校准方法。

abstract: [Pediatric annals] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming health care and has important implications for pediatric hospital medicine. Advances in machine learning and large language models have enabled applications that support patient care in the areas of clinical documentation, decision making, and prognostic modeling. Pediatric AI systems leverage diverse data sources, including electronic health records, medical imaging, physiologic monitoring, wearable devices, and genomic data. Current applications include AI-powered scribes, chart summarization, clinical decision support, prediction of sepsis and clinical deterioration, precision pharmacotherapy, rare disease diagnosis, and mental health interventions. These technologies have demonstrated potential to reduce clinician workload, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and facilitate earlier therapeutic interventions. However, significant challenges remain, including limited and heterogeneous pediatric datasets by virtue of age and developmental characteristics in children, bias, privacy concerns, lack of representativeness, and the need for rigorous validation and oversight. As AI adoption expands, pediatric hospitalists require foundational knowledge of AI principles and limitations to ensure safe, equitable, and effective implementation. With appropriate governance and multidisciplinary collaboration, AI has the potential to improve pediatric inpatient outcomes and health care delivery.

abstract: [Pediatric annals] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing pediatric inpatient care, extending beyond clinical applications to many areas of health care delivery, medical education, and research. Studies suggest that families are receptive to AI-assisted care if transparency, human oversight, and shared decision making are maintained. Effective governance is necessary to address concerns related to accountability, privacy, regulatory gaps, postdeployment monitoring, and equitable implementation. Algorithmic bias, data representativeness, informed consent, and the potential for AI to exacerbate health care disparities pose new ethical concerns. Explainable AI may improve transparency, trust, and acceptance by clinicians through making AI-generated recommendations more understandable. AI can also transform medical education through personalized learning, simulation, and clinical decision support, while requiring new competencies in AI literacy. AI offers opportunities to expedite clinical trials and data analysis but requires pediatric-specific frameworks to address age-related bias and emphasize ethical use of pediatric data in research. Responsible implementation, strong oversight, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continued clinician leadership will be essential to realizing AI's potential while safeguarding the welfare of pediatric patients and their families.

abstract: [Research square] Introduction Sepsis-induced organ dysfunction remains a leading cause of mortality in critical care. While recent evidence suggests that Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) may improve outcomes, significant heterogeneity among septic patient populations in prior trials might have contributed to mixed responses and thus fueled clinical skepticism. To address this challenge and to model TPE effectiveness across varying levels of sepsis severity, we utilized a time-dependent, 8-state transition Markov model integrated with a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) framework. Methods An AI-generated "digital twin" cohort (N = 10,000) was randomized 1:1 to standard care (SC) or adjuvant TPE groups. Transition probabilities were parameterized using a pooled relative risk (RR) of 0.58, derived from five recent meta-analyses. The model incorporated specific hazard multipliers for acute kidney injury (AKI; 1.5x), thrombocytopenia (1.3x), and high-dose vasopressor requirements (1.25x). Patient flow was simulated through eight clinically defined health states over a 28-day horizon. Outcomes included 28-day survival, absolute risk reduction (ARR), and number needed to treat (NNT) stratified by Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score quartiles (8, 12, 16, and 20). Bayesian methods were employed to determine survival probabilities and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI). Results Across the modelled full 10,000-patient cohort, TPE increased 28 day survival compared to standard care (67.3% vs. 44.7%). The survival benefit was modest in the group with the lowest degree of organ failure (SOFA 8) (TPE 87.6% vs. SC 78.4%; ARR 9.2%; NNT 11). However, this benefit was more pronounced in cases of higher burden of organ failure, particularly within the SOFA 20 cohort (TPE 48.8% vs. SC 12.8%; ARR 36%; NNT 3) and in cases with AKI + thrombocytopenia + higher doses of vasopressors (ARR 36%; NNT 3). For SOFA 20 patients, TPE was associated with a 38% reduction in the hazard of death (HR 0.62; 95% CrI 0.54-0.71). Conclusion These simulation results suggests that the efficacy of TPE might be dependent on baseline illness severity. While the clinical impact is more limited in moderate sepsis (SOFA 8), TPE appears to offer a profound survival advantage and high therapeutic yield for patients with multi-organ failure.
